transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Liam (HelioSpark), Sara (Helio infra), Devon (PM)
Links shared: onboarding deck (drive.redwood/onboard-helio), pilot spec sheet (sheet.redwood/pilot-helio), security pack (link to pdf)

00:00 Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining happy new year, we'll kick off quick, purpose of today's session is to align on constraints and a two week pilot to prove perf & cost.
01:02 Liam: yeah thanks, quick context - we run ML infra for a SaaS analytics product. currently in-house inference on g4/v2 clusters, latency very spiky at peak, token costs are high and ops overhead is heavy. goal is reduce p50 latency to <120ms for user prompts and lower per-token cost ~20-30%.
02:10 Sara: infra constraints — we need data resident in us-east-1, SOC2 required, and we have a managed KMS/HSM for key wrapping. VPC peering or private link is prefered, but we can consider dedicated infra if latency is predictable.
03:20 Jonas: quick note — Redwood supports three deployment modes: Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem). For pilot we usually start with Dedicated or Private depending on network constraints. We'll ask for a small benchmark using sample prompts.
04:15 Devon: timeline — we'd like pilot in the next two weeks, decision on production in 6 weeks. Key stakeholders: security, infra, ML team. Success metric: latency p50 <120ms, throughput 50 req/s sustained, and cost per 1k tokens under target.
05:40 Maya: sounds good. quick qual questions - what model family are you testing today, and what's your typical sequence length?
06:05 Liam: mostly instruction tuned Llama variants and an in-house fine-tune. Typical seq len 256 but some longer at 1024 for batch summarization.
06:45 Jonas: okay that helps for kernel selection and batch profiles — we will recommend quantized variants and look at KV cache behavior for longer seqs. Note: our runtime does continuous batching and KV caching but we need realistic sample traffic.
08:30 Sara: about security - can you outline audit logging, key mgmt, and where logs are retained? we have strict retention and SSO is mandatory.
09:05 Maya: sure - we have audit logs in the Console, retention options (30/90/365 days), SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, and KMS integrations for Private (bring-your-own key). We'll share SOC2 and ISO certs after this call.
10:40 Devon: any issues with PII in prompts? we will route customer data to inference, need redaction or allowlist.
11:15 Jonas: we support on-client redaction and also server-side redaction hooks; can instrument a PRF to scrub sensitive fields before sending. We'll include pattern examples for your QA.
12:00 Maya: ok next the pilot shape: small production-like workload — 50 concurrent users, target 50 req/s sustained for an hour, a mix of seq lengths, and a set of 30 eval prompts to measure quality regressions. we will measure latency, token cost, and tail SLOs.
14:20 Liam: for evaluation, we need to be sure quantization doesn't break accuracy. how do you detect quality regressions?
15:00 Jonas: Redwood Optimize offers quality monitoring tied to evals/prompt sets; we'll run a baseline model and compare token-accuracy and n-gram drift, plus we can keep a canary policy to fallback to higher-precision model if regressions exceed threshold.
16:30 Sara: networking — we prefer VPC peering but have strict egress rules, any transit through public internet is a blocker.
17:05 Jonas: for Private, we run a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC and the inference nodes can be in the same network; for Dedicated we can offer private link peering as well. there are a couple of dirs for NAT traversal we need to validate.
19:10 Devon: cost vs latency tradeoff - what levers will we have?
19:30 Jonas: levers are quantization profile, batching config, prefix KV caching, and routing to a cheaper model variant. Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost plus latency per route so you can tune. For strict latency SLOs we can pin to a higher-capacity model or dedicated pool.
21:50 Liam: do you support HSM integration for KMS?
22:10 Maya: yes - we support customer KMS/HSM with Private installs; we'll include a KMS integration note in the security pack.
23:00 Sara: are there any compliance customers with similar needs you can reference?
23:35 Maya: yes we have a handful — we'll share anonymized case notes in the doc pack.
24:20 Devon: ok about canary and rollouts, we need automatic fallback to a stable model if latency spikes.
24:50 Jonas: we have rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to pinned variants if SLO breached. We'll draft a rollout playbook for the pilot.
26:30 Liam: about logs - how long, and do you ship to our SIEM?
27:00 Maya: we can forward audit logs to your SIEM, retention flexible; will document exact fields.
28:10 Sara: firewall - port requirements?
28:35 Jonas: minimal ports for agent + control plane, specifics in network checklist.
30:00 Maya: ok let's run through a quick risk checklist: data residency - confirmed us-east-1 for pilot; SLA expectations - pilot doesn't carry SLA but production Dedicated/Private can have SLA; Ops - who will be on-call during pilot?
31:15 Devon: our infra engineer (Sara) and one ML lead (Liam) will be on-call; Redwood SE to be on-call for benchmark window.
32:00 Maya: Priya (CSM) will coordinate runbooks and meeting cadence.
33:10 Priya: cadence proposed: daily async updates during pilot, 2x per week sync calls, and a final review at pilot end.
34:05 Liam: about model weights — we can't upload certain licensed weights off-prem, is there a way to run private model on your infra?
35:00 Jonas: for on-prem we can support Private deployment where model weights remain in your environment; otherwise Dedicated requires compatible licensing. We will map licensing constraints in the pilot plan.
37:20 Devon: okay sample data - we'll share a sanitized dataset and 30 eval prompts by EOD 2026-01-06.
38:05 Maya: great. Jonas, for the benchmark can you outline minimal scripts and metrics?
38:20 Jonas: yes - will provide a runbook with k6 load config, seq length distribution, and token accounting. we'll request ephemeral API keys for pilot.
40:15 Sara: one more on networking - we use strict private CIDR ranges, can you accommodate?
40:40 Jonas: yes, we'll validate with your networking team; need contact and expected IPs.
41:50 Liam: security review — do you have a standard SRF?
42:10 Maya: yes we have a security questionnaire; I'll attach to the pack.
43:30 Devon: will this pilot require large infra commits from our side?
44:00 Jonas: minimal — mostly access, network peering or VPN, and sample data. If you choose Dedicated we will plan capacity but pilot can be small.
45:10 Priya: action recap in a sec.
45:20 Maya: ok let's capture final agreement: pilot window target 2026-01-12 to 2026-01-14 (bench run), prep this week, deliverables: security pack, pilot runbook, sample scripts, and SOW draft.
46:45 Devon: agreed. who will own the network contact?
47:10 Sara: i'll own it and share details by 2026-01-07.
47:30 Maya: i'll send security pack and SOW draft by 2026-01-08/09. Jonas you'll prepare runbook by 2026-01-11.
48:15 Jonas: yes.
48:40 Liam: any blockers from Redwood side we should be aware of?
48:55 Maya: none immediate; licensing for model weights could be the only blocker if you need a non-distributable model weight. we'll map alternatives.
50:00 Priya: ok we'll schedule the technical deep dive for Jan 11 - invite to follow.
50:40 Maya: and i'll put the pilot tracker in the shared drive.
51:05 Devon: thanks everyone, good session.
56:30 Maya: quick close - next steps and action items in chat, we will follow up over email.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had a few mis-heard terms: "KV cache" sometimes appears as "KV cash", "Dedicated" as "Dedicaed"; proper nouns may be slightly off.

End of transcript.
